I have to change my review for this game to negative. When this game came out a year ago it was $50. They sold the DLC which I figured I would wait for since it looked pretty basic, but never got around to it. Now they are selling an ultimate version for $40. And if you paid the $50 you get a discount on the DLC. So you would pay about $11. So people who supported the game at release get to pay overall $60. I saw someone ask on Facebook if they would upgrade users since now only a year later its all combined. They just said we get a discount. Pretty lame.

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

If you like souls-like games and you are up for a challenge then this is your game. I tried with both controlled and mouse/keyboard, but I preferred controller. While it is a shooter and you do get more damage for head shots, it doesn't seem like there is too much of a difference. If head shots were instant kills I would do mouse/keyboard but its not. The enemies do have weak spots, but if you lock on with a controller and maneuver you can hit it. I like the weapon variety and leveling system. The environment of the game really pulled me in. And the difficulty at times really pissed me off. But it was so satisfying when I got past. Looks like the price is lower no that when I purchased it. I think that price is a bit more fair because it does lack the whole changing of outfits and armor like dark souls. And some bosses are reused. But it was fun and very difficult. However I have not bought the dlc map and don't plan on it unless the price goes down. Looking at the videos it doesn't look much different than the original game. While I enjoy the game I don't imagine anything else or more gameplay can make it more enjoyable. It was a good length as it was. I would rather have a sequel with ability to change armor/pickup armor and some pvp and co-op elements.

This is a Dark Souls-style third person shooter. This means the RPG and level design elements are lifted straight from Dark Souls; the storytelling is mysterious and minimal but lore-heavy, like Dark Souls; the inventory system and item usage is just like Dark Souls. But the combat is focused on gun-play, with melee limited to a quick 1-2 combo with dual-wielded weapons.

Like Dark Souls, you will die a lot in the first few hours, and the deaths will feel cheap. This is not actually the case; all of the enemies adhere to strict patterns, like in Dark Souls, and once you've learned them, you can exploit them mercilessly. There are a few spikes in difficulty at times, but nothing you can't overcome with some patience.

The performance has some issues on an average rig, but the game seems to run fine so long as you turn down the shadows, which does not impact the visuals too heavily, due to the foggy, gloomy style of the game.

The game boasts an interesting and dark sci-fantasy setting, solid sound design, solid voice acting and outright decent music, responsive controls (especially if you're using mouse and keyboard - the shooting feels just right, and you can shoot enemy limbs to stagger or disarm them), and a pretty distinctive art direction.

Much like Dark Souls, this game may not instantly click with you. Like Dark Souls, the game may seem occasionally janky or eccentric (let's not forget the FPS-related horrors of Blight Town, people). But persevere, and like Dark Souls, you should find it a rewarding and entertaining experience.
Cool Souls like game. A mix between Dark Souls, Diablo, and Destiny. Impressed with how smooth and responsive gameplay is.

I beat this game only because I don't like getting half way through a game to drop it, feeling like I wasted my time.
Joke's on me though because it was a complete waste of my time.  The only 2 things I like about this game are the visuals and some of the music.  To sum up this game in one word I would say: TEDIOUS.  It was a real slog after the first couple hours as I fought bullet sponge after bullet sponge, just to get to some pathetic boss that looks very much like the last one and beat them first try.  It doesn't feel quite right on either controller or KB&M.  The people saying it feels "clunky" are correct, as I can't find a better word to explain jerky action.
Many of the normal enemies are harder than the bosses.  The enemy placement is also "just so" that can't really skip most of them.  It feels like its just game padding.  Add all that up with an extremely sub par ending and no, I don't recommend this game.  Don't waste your time. I've wasted mine to save you from this.
It's OK. But unbalanced and the camera control is not very good.
